t:
Section 9(3) of the Belarus Democracy Act of 2004 (22 U.S.C. 5811 note) is amended—
    (1) in subparagraph (A), by inserting “governors, heads of state enterprises,” after “Chairmen of State Committees,”; and 
    (2) in subparagraph (B)—
        (A) by striking “who is” and inserting the following: “who—“(i) is”; 
        (B) by striking “and” at the end and inserting “or”; and 
        (C) by adding at the end the following new clause:“(ii) is otherwise engaged in public corruption in Belarus; and”.

fable.w: This section only amends a definition in the Belarus Democracy Act of 2004, expanding the category of Belarusian officials covered and adding those engaged in public corruption. The mention of "governors" and "heads of state enterprises" could be misread as involving outside parties, but they are foreign officials being defined as targets of the Act, not parties consulted before a federal decision. Nothing here provides for comment, hearings, advisory bodies, consultation with non-federal entities, rulemaking, or a right to sue.

opus.w: This amendment only widens a definition in the Belarus Democracy Act, so that Belarusian governors, heads of state enterprises and corrupt officials count as senior leadership of the Government of Belarus. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. 'Governors' here are the people the definition covers, not participants in a federal decision, so the keyword reading fails.

These words only widen the Act's definition of senior Belarusian government officials, and add officials "engaged in public corruption in Belarus." Nobody is consulted, there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue, and no outside party takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the definitions of individuals subject to sanctions under the Belarus Democracy Act. It expands the list of covered persons to include governors, heads of state enterprises, and those engaged in public corruption. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, comment, hearing, or participation by outside parties in the decision-making process. The mention of 'public corruption' refers to the conduct of the sanctioned individuals, not to public participation in the government's decision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 9(3) of the Belarus Democracy Act of 2004 (22 U.S.C. 5811 note) is amended— (1) in subparagraph (A), by inserting “governors, heads of state enterprises,” after “Chairmen of State Committees,”; and (2) in subparagraph (B)— (A) by striking “who is” and inserting the following: “who—“(i) is”; (B) by striking “and” at the end and inserting “or”; and (C) by adding at the end the following new clause:“(ii) is otherwise engaged in public corruption in Belarus; and”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "public corruption," it implies some form of public oversight or participation. However, the text is purely definitional, amending the criteria for sanctions against specific individuals. It does not establish any process for the public or outside entities to participate in the decision-making process regarding those sanctions.
